name: tirith
description: Defensive AI security assessment and remediation for your own repos and web apps: scan, validate exploitability in an isolated lab, and open fix pull requests.

interface.shortDescription: Breach your lab, then fix it
interface.longDescription: Tirith watches over the code and web apps you own. It runs Semgrep, Gitleaks, Trivy and a passive ZAP baseline, explains each finding in plain language, checks exploitability with fixed non-destructive tests in an isolated lab with dummy data, and opens fix pull requests that a human reviews. Every action is limited to an allow-listed scope and recorded in an audit log.
defaultPrompt: Start with me: which box should Tirith look at first?
Breach the demo box and show me what gives.
What is the worst thing still open right now?

commands.name: start
commands.description: Onboarding: scope, mode, what to run first
commands.prompt: Walk me through onboarding: your current mode and posture, then ask me for the one target to start with (repo, host, or url), and confirm it is in scope before touching anything.

commands.name: hunt
commands.prompt: Hunt — mode 1 on {{target}}: scan it, reproduce every finding with a control request first, and only keep what actually reproduces. Finish with the as-found report.

commands.name: hunt-and-fix
commands.description: Mode 2: same, then fix and open PRs
commands.prompt: Hunt and fix — mode 2 on {{target}}: same proof work as mode 1, switch to assisted, fix the confirmed issues, verify each one and open a PR for review.

commands.name: breach-demo
commands.prompt: Breach the demo box on localhost:8090 end to end and prove each flaw with a control and one payload.

commands.name: status
commands.prompt: What is my current posture and mode, and what are the ten worst open findings with their proof state?

commands.name: report
commands.description: Rebuild the last report as HTML
commands.prompt: Render the as-found and as-fixed report for my latest assessment.

commands.name: reset
commands.prompt: Stop any running analysis and put the demo box on 127.0.0.1:8090 back to its original state.
